item.title: Catholic bishops declare nationwide fasting, prayer
item.description: The Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria, CBCN, has declared a nationwide prayer and fasting programme to promote free, fair, credible and peaceful elections in 2027. The programme, themed ‘Let Justice and Peace Flow’, is drawn from Amos 5:24. The bishops announced the initiative in a statement signed by their President, Archbishop Matthew Ndagoso, and Secretary, Bishop Peter Odetoyinbo, yesterday in Abuja. They said the programme was necessary as Nigeria approached the 2027 general elections amid recurring challenges of electoral violence, rigging, vote-buying and ethno-religious divisions. The bishops urged dioceses, parishes, church societies, prayer groups, families and individuals to participate actively in the spiritual exercise. They said the initiative was aimed at seeking God’s guidance for electoral officials and security personnel to discharge their responsibilities faithfully, while inspiring citizens to vote conscientiously and discouraging electoral malpractice and violence. According to the statement, all parishes would observe October 31 and November 28 as days of prayer and fasting for Nigeria. Activities would include fasting, the Rosary procession, Holy Mass and the recitation of the CBCN prayer for the 2027 elections. The bishops also designated December 8, the Solemnity of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, as a nationwide diocesan day of prayer. The programme would begin with Holy Mass at 3 p.m., presided over by the diocesan bishop, during which a pastoral letter titled “2027 Elections: Call to Responsible Choice and Action” would be read. The Mass would be followed by a Rosary procession to the cathedral at 4:30 p.m. and conclude with Eucharistic Benediction. The statement further declared January 15, 2027, the eve of the general elections, a nationwide parish day of prayer and fasting. The bishops urged Nigerians to reject tribalism, corruption, bribery and voter apathy, while encouraging citizens to vote and protect their votes peacefully. They called for a credible electoral process free from rancour and bloodshed. The post Catholic bishops declare nationwide fasting, prayer appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Buhari: If a general couldn’t wipe out insecurity, spare Tinubu —Yari
item.description: The Director-General of All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has said President Bola Tinubu should not be blamed solely for the widespread insecurity in the country. Yari, who stated this during a visit to Kebbi, where he met with Governor Nasir Idris, traditional rulers and other party leaders in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, yesterday, said ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, a retired general, did his best but could not tackle insecurity completely. Nevertheless, the President has done his utmost best to address the security challenges confronting the country,” he said. item.title: Doctors top global trust rankings as politicians, influencers come last
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Medical doctors, scientists and teachers are the most trusted professions globally, while politicians and social media influencers rank among the least trusted, according to a survey of 23,530 online adults under 75 across 32 countries. The survey, known as the Ipsos Global Trustworthiness Index 2026, conducted by Ipsos, an international market research and public opinion polling company, showed that doctors lead the rankings, with 58 percent of respondents expressing trust in them, followed by scientists at 56 percent and teachers at 54 percent. Restaurant serving staff ranked fourth at 44 percent, followed by the armed forces at 43 percent. Police officers, judges and ordinary men and women each recorded 38 percent, while lawyers received 31 percent. Television news anchors recorded 30 percent, while pollsters and clergy or priests each scored 29 percent. Taxi drivers and civil servants followed at 28 percent. Journalists and bankers each recorded 27 percent, while business leaders scored 26 percent. At the lower end, government ministers recorded 20 per cent, followed by advertising executives at 19 per cent. Social media influencers and politicians generally ranked last, with 15 per cent each. The percentages represent the share of respondents expressing trust in each profession or group, not those selecting it as their single most trusted occupation. The precise survey question and response options should be verified against the original Ipsos report. The findings highlight a marked contrast between trust in health and scientific professionals and confidence in political figures and social surveys. item.title: Gunmen kill at least 40 civilians in Mali
item.description: More than 40 civilians have been killed in weekend attacks by armed men on camps in Mali’s northeastern Menaka region, security and community sources told AFP on Monday. The assailants reportedly rode in on motorcycles, targeting camps mainly housing members of the Daoussahak community, whose executive bureau blamed the killings on the Islamic State group. item.title: Kenyan pastor, who told followers to starve for Jesus, convicted of 191 murders
item.description: A Kenyan court has convicted pastor Paul Mackenzie of murdering 191 people, including 190 children, after he allegedly directed members of his religious group to starve themselves and their children to death to “meet Jesus”. The BBC reported on Monday that 28 other leaders of the religious group were also convicted of murder. All the defendants had pleaded not guilty, repeatedly maintaining that nobody had been forced to die. Delivering an eight-hour judgement in the coastal city of Mombasa, Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie’s followers regarded him as “Jesus’s mouthpiece”. According to the report, one of Mackenzie’s co-accused told the court that the pastor had instructed followers to use violence against anyone who refused to fast. The co-accused said anyone who “resisted the directive to fast must be forced to go to heaven through kicks and blows”. The judge also revealed that burials in the forest where the group operated were referred to as “weddings”, with those who died described as people who “were celebrated as having wedded with Jesus”. The court heard that 17 men from a nearby town were hired to excavate shallow graves in the forest, with some reportedly receiving as little as $8 (£6) a day. One of the gravediggers, identified as James, recounted the disturbing discoveries made during the exercise. “Every grave we found had at least three bodies,” James told the BBC. “Some of the remains were of children as young as a few weeks old.” He added, “We once found 12 bodies of children in a line inside a grave. It was massive, the bodies were arranged like clothes. One on top of another.” The workers also reported finding children whose “hands and legs tied and bodies wrapped in bedsheets”. But it was so planned and secretive that nobody could tell what was happening inside,” Karisa said. It was massive, the bodies were arranged like clothes. One on top of another.” The workers also reported finding children whose “hands and legs tied and bodies wrapped in bedsheets”. Another gravedigger, Salim Karisa, said some of the victims were known to residents of neighbouring Shakahola town, as members of the group regularly visited to purchase supplies and collect water from the River Galana. “We would sometimes carry people on our motorbikes into the forest. But it was so planned and secretive that nobody could tell what was happening inside,” Karisa said. Mackenzie established Good News International Ministries in 2003, building a following of thousands over the next 16 years through church branches across Kenya. The church also ran a television station, Times TV, which aired his sermons from Malindi. His teachings reportedly described education as “evil”, healthcare as “against the doctrine” and digital identity cards as “the mark of the devil”. Mackenzie’s son, Dan Paul Mackenzie, said he worked as a cameraperson for the church and recalled how worship services were organised. “The children would sit at the back, adults in the middle, and everyone would sing worship songs all morning,” he said. The pastor usually began preaching at noon, with some sessions featuring what was described as “casting out demons”. After the church’s main branch shut down in 2019, Mackenzie relocated to Shakahola forest and encouraged his followers to move there. Among those who followed him was Peter Shukrani, 23, who relocated to the forest with his mother. He had joined the church at the age of eight and considered Mackenzie his “spiritual father”. Despite his experiences, Shukrani said he would “never say a bad word about him”. However, he fell ill while living in the forest, where medication was prohibited. His condition worsened after his mother discarded the medicines he needed. “My mother would throw away all the medicine I was supposed to take because she believe that only God could heal me,” Shukrani said. He described the group’s living conditions, saying members stayed in mud houses scattered across the expansive forest. “We lived a quiet normal life, fasting for a few days then having a small meal,” he said. The first bodies were discovered by local herders in March 2023, by which time hundreds of people had reportedly died. Karisa said some victims were so severely weakened by starvation that they died while being transported out of the forest. “We would carry someone out of the forest but they were so frail that they would die in our arms,” he said. Shukrani was among those rescued. He said he had been bedridden for weeks before his rescue and believed he would not have survived without intervention. “My mother believed Pastor Mackenzie’s doctrine that medicine was evil. I would have died if I wasn’t rescued from Shakahola forest,” he said. Many of the recovered bodies remain unidentified because of decomposition. Court records reportedly identify several victims as “unknown male child”, using the locations of their graves and the dates of discovery to distinguish them. Despite accounts of starvation, strangulation and bludgeoning among the victims, Shukrani continued to defend Mackenzie before the verdict. He described the pastor as “a good person who cares for me”. “Mackenzie didn’t force anyone to fast. People made those choices by themselves because of their beliefs. I still love him and he is still my pastor,” Shukrani said. Dan Mackenzie, however, argued before the ruling that his father should be held responsible for the deaths because of his leadership position within the group. “He was the leader, he was someone who they were looking [up to]. So he is a murderer of mass killing,” he said. The post Kenyan pastor, who told followers to starve for Jesus, convicted of 191 murders appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Customs to review complaints of 397 rejected recruitment applicants
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has announced plans to review complaints by applicants who were disqualified during its recent recruitment screening exercise despite appearing on the shortlist for training. The Service said the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, ordered a case-by-case review after meeting with some of the aggrieved applicants. In a statement signed by the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller of Customs Abdullahi Maiwada, on Monday, the NCS said the review was aimed at ensuring that legitimate complaints were examined while maintaining the integrity of the recruitment process. It explained that appearing on the final shortlist did not automatically guarantee enlistment, as applicants were required to undergo several stages of verification, including credential checks, physical fitness assessments, medical examinations, age verification and drug screening. According to the Service, screening irregularities involving 397 applicants were identified in areas including substance use, physical fitness, medical records, age and submitted documentation. It added that some candidates were also disqualified over irregularities identified in their selection process. The NCS urged affected applicants who believe they were unfairly disqualified to submit their details and complaints to helpdesk@customs.gov.ng for review. It said applicants seeking reconsideration would be subjected to fresh screening, stressing that the review would not automatically guarantee admission into the training college. The Service further warned that applicants found to have engaged in criminal conduct, including certificate fraud and other offences, would be referred for appropriate legal action and prosecution. It urged the affected candidates and the general public to remain calm and use the designated channel to submit their complaints. The post Customs to review complaints of 397 rejected recruitment applicants appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Close up your borders’ – Trump blames French unrest on immigration
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday again blamed immigration for protests and violence that have rocked France in recent days, urging Europe and French President Emmanuel Macron to tighten borders. “What’s happening in France has to do with immigration, not schools, not anything,” Trump told reporters in Washington, echoing his comments from the day before. “It’s immigration, and I told President Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders.” Weekend demonstrations over soaring prices were held in Paris and other cities, degenerating into some of the worst street violence France has seen in recent years. Trump recounted a conversation with Macron, telling him “a long time ago, you’re making a big mistake in France. You’re letting everybody from the world come in. The whole world was coming in. “Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon,” the 80-year-old Republican added. “If Europe doesn’t close its borders and bring the criminals out, like the people that are protesting, Europe is finished.” Trump made combating illegal immigration a central pledge of his 2024 campaign, at times relying on false claims that played on racial fears. item.title: Maddison shines as Tottenham claim long-awaited first PL win of season
item.description: James Maddison made a sensational return to Tottenham’s starting line-up after 17 months away on Monday as Spurs beat Coventry 3-1 to claim their long-awaited first Premier League win of the season. The England midfielder has featured only fleetingly since May 2025, when he suffered the first of two serious knee injuries. But Maddison needed less than a quarter of an hour to put Spurs ahead at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with a stunning first-time strike from outside the penalty area. Jack Rudoni levelled early in the second half but the home side were back in front just before the hour mark when Omar Marmoush lashed home his first goal for the club and substitute Ben Davies made the points safe late on. Roberto De Zerbi’s team came into the match bottom of the Premier League and with the unwanted record of being the only team in England’s top six divisions without a league win this season despite a huge summer spend. The Spurs boss had taken his squad to Marbella in southern Spain for some warm-weather training in a bid to kickstart their season. He named Maddison in his starting line-up while Sweden midfielder Dejan Kulusevski returned to the matchday squad for the first time in 17 months. Maddison ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in August 2025, just three months after injuring the same knee. The 29-year-old wasted little time in making his mark, putting his side ahead in the 14th minute in spectacular style after fine work from Mohammed Kudus on the right. Maddison, lurking just outside the penalty area, received the ball from Kudus and sent it curling past Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and into the top corner, sparking wild scenes of delight among the home fans. Tottenham now had their tails up and threatened to overwhelm the visitors but Frank Lampard’s newly promoted Coventry, who had won their previous two games, re-established a foothold. Maddison went close to putting Spurs 2-0 after half an hour but his half-cross, half-shot curled narrowly wide. But they failed to stretch their lead and Coventry were level in the 49th minute, courtesy of a Rudoni strike from close range. Spurs lost the ball in the Coventry half and the visitors swept forward. Rudoni’s cross hit a teammate but the ball fell kindly for him and he drove home. Just nine minutes later Spurs were back in front when former Manchester City forward Marmoush held off Milan van Ewijk before unleashing an unstoppable shot. Kulusevski, who suffered a knee injury in May 2025, was introduced in the final minutes to a huge ovation from the home fans. Spurs veteran Davies made the three points safe deep into added time, poking home from the edge of the penalty area as Tottenham could at last relax. Maddison ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in August 2025, just three months after injuring the same knee. The 29-year-old wasted little time in making his mark, putting his side ahead in the 14th minute in spectacular style after fine work from Mohammed Kudus on the right. Maddison, lurking just outside the penalty area, received the ball from Kudus and sent it curling past Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and into the top corner, sparking wild scenes of delight among the home fans. Tottenham now had their tails up and threatened to overwhelm the visitors but Frank Lampard’s newly promoted Coventry, who had won their previous two games, re-established a foothold. Maddison went close to putting Spurs 2-0 after half an hour but his half-cross, half-shot curled narrowly wide. But they failed to stretch their lead and Coventry were level in the 49th minute, courtesy of a Rudoni strike from close range. Spurs lost the ball in the Coventry half and the visitors swept forward. Rudoni’s cross hit a teammate but the ball fell kindly for him and he drove home. Just nine minutes later Spurs were back in front when former Manchester City forward Marmoush held off Milan van Ewijk before unleashing an unstoppable shot. Kulusevski, who suffered a knee injury in May 2025, was introduced in the final minutes to a huge ovation from the home fans. Spurs veteran Davies made the three points safe deep into added time, poking home from the edge of the penalty area as Tottenham could at last relax. item.title: Florida issues arrest warrant for Cuba’s ex-leader Raul Castro
item.description: Florida’s top prosecutor announced an arrest warrant Monday for former Cuban president Raul Castro on state murder charges that echo a federal indictment unveiled earlier this year. Raul Castro, 95, is wanted on murder charges connected to the February 24, 1996 shooting down of two civilian aircraft from “Brothers to the Rescue,” an organization assisting Cubans fleeing to the US state by sea. “Raul Castro ordered the murder of four Floridians in cold blood, and Florida will never stop pursuing accountability for that communist conspiracy,” Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said in a statement. Castro, brother of the late revolutionary leader and US nemesis Fidel Castro, was indicted on federal charges related to the incident in May. The move came as President Donald Trump’s right-wing administration steadily ramped up economic, political and legal pressure on the Cuban communist government. “We’re committed to pursuing every lawful, prosecutable avenue to bring accountability, including parallel federal and state prosecutions,” US Attorney Jason A. Reding Quinones said in a statement supporting Florida’s action. “We’re proud to stand with Florida in seeking justice for the four Americans murdered in the Brothers to the Rescue shootdown nearly 30 years ago,” the federal prosecutor said. In a statement on X, Cuba’s Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez condemned “the latest futile maneuver by anti-Cuban politicians in South Florida,” which he said was a “reflection of political rot and moral collapse.” Trump previously seized on a US indictment to justify military action in January that toppled Venezuela’s then-president Nicolas Maduro, a staunch ally of the Cuban authorities. Current Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel has said the US federal indictment against Castro has “no legal basis” and was an attempt “to justify the folly of a military aggression against Cuba.” AFP The post Florida issues arrest warrant for Cuba’s ex-leader Raul Castro appeared first on Vanguard News .

The competition was held as part of the “Project for Establishing a Startup Digital Innovation Academy to Support Youth and SME Innovation Growth in Nigeria,” supported by the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), with the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) as the partner agency. The project is being implemented by a consortium consisting of Soongsil University, Maincontents, and Eduniety Lab. The final round was graced by H.E. Jung Yo-an, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Nigeria; Senator John Owan Enoh, Honourable Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment; Mr. Blessed Chirimuta, Deputy Resident Representative, UNDP Nigeria; Mr. Charles O. Odii, Director General and CEO of SMEDAN; Dabureje Onesi-Lawani, Director of Monitoring and Evaluation, SMEDAN; and Mr. Kim Eun-seop, Country Director of the KOICA Nigeria Office. From 3,856 applicants to 10 teams The first cohort of ACE Startup Academy opened with 3,856 applications. Of these, 120 teams were selected for the training programme for aspiring entrepreneurs and completed courses in business modelling and digital and AI capability. Forty-five of the teams that finished the training advanced to the preliminary round, held over two days on 7 and 8 October. The 10 teams that came through the preliminaries took to the stage for the final. The final round ran as a pitch and question-and-answer session for each team, assessed on site by five judges. The panel was chaired by Mrs. Ifeanyi Iloh of Ventures Park, with two judges from SMEDAN, one from Steady Anchor Limited and one from the KOICA Nigeria Office. A finalist pitches before the judges during the final round at the E-Government Training Centre, Abuja. Run on an online judging solution Both the preliminary and final rounds were run and judged on an online judging solution developed by Lim Han- kyu, CEO of Maincontents, who joined the project as a competition operations specialist. Teams uploaded everything needed for their pitch — IR decks, MVPs and demo video links — directly to the solution, and judges opened those materials on the same screen while scoring on their laptops. Entry, document collection, scoring and tallying were all handled within a single system. Instead of collecting paper score sheets and adding them up by hand, results were compiled the moment a pitch ended, and the full scoring record was retained. On the day of the final, tallying was completed as soon as the tenth team finished presenting, allowing the awards ceremony to follow immediately. “The judging solution finishes the tallying on site, and at the same time it gathers the pitch decks, the MVPs and the comments the judges leave, all in one place,” Lim said. “Once that is analysed into each team’s strengths and areas to improve, it becomes the starting material for the incubation stage.” Loghema takes the Grand Prize The Grand Prize of US$5,000 went to Loghema, an AI service that recognises scripture references spoken during a sermon and puts the verse on screen within seconds. The team built it around a familiar problem: by the time the media operator has found the passage and chosen a translation, the preacher has already moved on. It is targeting the more than 100,000 churches in Nigeria. The official poster for the ACE Startup Academy 2026 Pitch Competition Final. The Excellence Award of US$3,000 went to Tita Universal Services Ltd, an AI platform that generates lecture timetables for tertiary institutions. It aims to reduce the room clashes and omitted courses that arise where timetables are still drawn up by hand. The Merit Award of US$2,000 went to Tiptop Tutors, a virtual science laboratory that lets secondary school students repeat chemistry, physics and biology practicals where equipment and lab time are scarce. Its app, HandyLab, has students choose each step of an experiment, take measurements with virtual apparatus, receive immediate feedback and try again, and offers both a guided mode and a self-paced mode. It also works offline, in recognition of unreliable internet access. Encouragement Awards of US$1,000 each went to OneClickMed, which connects patient records across health facilities; Ikor, an AI writing tool that runs entirely offline on low-end devices; and Gyronics, developer of Axol, a wearable interface that allows people with upper-limb disabilities to control their devices. Challenge Awards of US$500 each went to Acclusivo; Saipris, which identifies struggling students early using performance data schools already hold; Monovella, which links women’s health management with specialist appointments; and Meertech Ltd, which catches export documentation errors before shipment. With a total prize fund of US$15,000, all 10 finalists received an award. Making sure everyone starts from the same line Sign language interpretation was provided throughout the competition, from the preliminaries to the final, to support the participation of Acclusivo, a deaf-led startup. That support will continue through the incubation programme and the visit to Korea. Acclusivo is led by Victor Oricha, who is deaf and serves as founder and CTO. DeafLMS, the platform the team is developing, is a visual-first STEM learning platform for deaf children that brings a lesson otherwise scattered across the teacher, the interpreter, the textbook and the screen into a single visual environment. From training to competition The training programme for aspiring entrepreneurs that preceded the competition consisted of a business model (BM) track and an AI and digital innovation track. A BM curriculum running from problem definition and customer validation through value proposition, revenue model and financial planning was delivered alongside data and AI practicals. The training was carried out together with local instructors and mentors developed through the training of trainers (ToT) programme that the Soongsil University consortium ran in the early phase of the project. Mentors who completed the ToT also took part in running this competition. Next: incubation, then Seoul The 10 finalists will join the ACE centre’s incubation programme for mentoring and hands-on coaching. One member from each team will then travel to Korea to experience the country’s startup and investment ecosystems first-hand, visiting companies and taking part in an IR demo day before investors. The competition is therefore not an end point but one stage in ACE’s growth pathway, which links training, selection, incubation and investment. The project aims to support innovation-driven growth for Nigerian youth and SMEs and to establish a sustainable digital startup ecosystem through the ACE operational model.

item.title: Photos: Billionaire Okoya’s son ties the knot in private ceremony
item.description: Idris Okoya, son of billionaire industrialist and Eleganza Group chairman Razaq Okoya, has married his partner, Rukoyah, in a private wedding ceremony. Shade Okoya, the industrialist’s wife, announced the union on Monday through an Instagram Story, where she shared a photograph of the newlyweds and congratulated them. “Congratulations to the newest couple @idrisokoya.” Shade was also seen in a video from the ceremony wearing aso ebi, the coordinated traditional attire worn by guests at the wedding. Photo: Yusluv Media Tuwo Pama International, a food vendor, also shared footage from the private event on Sunday, accompanying the video with prayers for the newly married couple. “Today’s event at Rukoyah and Idris Okoya’s wedding. May Almighty Allah bless their union,” the vendor wrote. Photo: Yusluv Media Idris is one of Razaq Okoya’s sons from an earlier marriage. His father founded the Eleganza Group, a Nigerian conglomerate with interests in manufacturing and other businesses. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s ethnic, religious appeal won’t work in North – Iliyasu Kwankwaso
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Musa Iliyasu Kwankwaso, has said former Vice President Atiku Abubakar cannot rely on ethnic and religious sentiments to win support in northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Kwankwaso said political dynamics in the North had changed, arguing that voters were increasingly concerned about leadership performance, development and issues affecting their daily lives. He made the position known in a signed statement on Monday. He insisted that Atiku lacked the level of acceptance and political influence once enjoyed in the region by the late President Muhammadu Buhari. “Atiku is not Buhari. He does not possess the size, stature and acceptance of the late Nigerian President to pose a threat to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Kwankwaso said. The APC chieftain argued that Atiku could no longer assume that Hausa-Fulani voters would support him based mainly on ethnic or regional considerations. “The North has gone beyond primordial sentiment, and his penchant for relying on the ethno-religious card will certainly fail him,” he said. Kwankwaso also questioned Atiku’s record during his eight years as vice president. He argued that the former vice president had yet to present a convincing account of the development achievements from his time in office. He maintained that the 2027 election would be shaped by voters’ expectations of better leadership and improved living conditions rather than ethnic or religious loyalties. The APC chieftain further alleged that Atiku’s political associates were aware of his limited influence among Hausa-Fulani voters. Kwankwaso expressed confidence that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu would remain a strong contender in the North despite efforts by opposition groups to build a regional coalition against him. item.title: Drone Strikes Across Sudan Kill More Than 100 People
item.description: A wave of drone strikes targeting war-torn Sudan’s army-held capital Khartoum and two western areas controlled by paramilitary forces has killed more than 100 people since Sunday, according to residents, medical workers and paramilitary sources. The deadliest drone strike hit near a market on Sunday evening in Al-Dibab town in the southwestern state of West Kordofan, which is controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that have been at war with Sudan’s military since April 2023. Residents and medical workers said a drone struck a transport hub where villagers had gathered after a market day to find rides home, killing 80 people. Ahmed Abakar Wadi, a resident who helped bury victims, told AFP at least 50 bodies were recovered at the scene, including that of his brother. Another 47 wounded people were taken to the nearby town of Al-Mujlad where 30 later died from their injuries, according to a medical source. “The drone struck once, and then came back 10 minutes later and struck again,” Wadi told AFP. The RSF’s self-declared administration, known as Tasis, and the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers accused the army of carrying out the attack. The military has not commented. The strike was one of the deadliest single attacks in Kordofan, an oil-rich region linking western and eastern Sudan where the army and the RSF have been battling for territory. AFP Hours later, early on Monday, another drone attack hit the RSF stronghold of Nyala, the capital of South Darfur. Medical and RSF sources said 17 people, including seven RSF officers, were killed and 23 wounded when a drone struck the city centre and destroyed two homes. On Monday morning, violence also reached the capital Khartoum, where a drone strike hit a house in a neighbourhood east of Khartoum airport, killing four people, including three children aged between two and six, according to a medical source. An army official said Sudanese air defences had intercepted drones launched by the RSF that were targeting the airport and nearby areas. In eastern Sudan, a military source said on Sunday that air defences also intercepted several RSF drones targeting the Atbara and Setit dams in Gadaref state, about 420 kilometres east of Khartoum. There is no definitive toll for Sudan’s conflict, but aid workers estimate it has killed more than 200,000 people and created what aid agencies describe as the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis. More than 1,100 people were killed in drone attacks across Sudan during the first half of this year alone, according to the United Nations. item.title: APM to Tinubu: You’re paying fuel subsidy through back door
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of paying fuel subsidy through the back door, questioning the recent petrol price reduction despite the government’s declaration that subsidy was gone. The party also dismissed Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele’s warning that restoring subsidy could push the naira to ₦4,000 per dollar, describing the projection as unfounded and accusing the government’s economic policies of driving businesses into closure. APM National Secretary, Ayodele Adebayo, stated this in a response to Vanguard’s inquiries, faulting the administration’s handling of fuel prices and its claims about investors’ loss of confidence in opposition parties. “What are they doing now with the current reduction in petrol price for one month? Is it not returning subsidy through the back door?” Adebayo asked. He argued that the naira had previously exchanged at a stronger rate, rejecting the minister’s projection as an attempt to justify the government’s position on subsidy. Adebayo also challenged Oyedele’s claim that investors had written off opposition parties as unserious, alleging that harsh economic policies had forced several companies to shut down. “Where are even the investors that the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, is talking about? Is it the recycled ones by the present administration?” he queried. The APM secretary said his party favoured an appropriate pricing framework for petroleum products to prevent further hardship, insisting that Nigerians should not be left with little money after paying for fuel. “We cannot subscribe to seeing Nigerians use all their entitlements and earnings to buy fuel due to harsh economic policies,” Adebayo said. item.title: Critic of Rwanda President Kagame beheaded in Uganda
item.description: A former Rwandan soldier living in Uganda, where he had become a vocal critic of his government back home, was found decapitated near Kampala, a police spokesperson said Monday. Rwandan authorities have been accused of assassinating opponents of President Paul Kagame, who has ruled the country with an iron fist since taking power in the aftermath of the 1994 genocide that claimed 800,000 lives, primarily among the Tutsi community. Robert Kabera, a former sergeant who fled Rwanda several years ago, was not outspoken during his time in the military but grew increasingly opposed to Kagame. His YouTube channel, “Major Robert TV”, which has 144,000 subscribers, included a song praising opposition figure Victoire Ingabire, a rare voice of dissent in Rwanda, who has been repeatedly imprisoned. Ugandan police said they were investigating the “murder of a male adult, (around 50), whose head was cut off, and up to now the head has not yet been recovered”, spokesperson Kituuma Rusoke told reporters on Monday, adding that the body had been identified by relatives as Robert Kabera. The body was found in Luwala, a village near Kampala, and the murder likely took place late on October 16 or early 17, he added. In Uganda, “Robert had no issues with anyone,” his brother, Victor Agaba, told AFP. “Our problem comes from home… The army created a criminal case against him. It was a witch hunt,” he said. Kabera was declared a fugitive after leaving Rwanda, and he was accused of corrupting a minor, which he denied. He is not the first opposition figure in exile to be assassinated. In 2021, a former lieutenant in the Rwandan army, Revocant Karemangingo, was shot dead in Mozambique, where he was suspected of secretly supporting an opposition force. Outspoken opponent Seif Bamporiki was gunned down in South Africa the same year, while a former Rwandan intelligence-chief-turned-critic, Patrick Karegeya, was strangled in his South African hotel room in 2014. Another exile, former general Faustin Kayumba Nyamwasa, who co-founded the Rwanda National Congress (RNC) opposition party with Karegeya, has survived several assassination attempts. item.content:encoded: A former Rwandan soldier living in Uganda, where he had become a vocal critic of his government back home, was found decapitated near Kampala, a police spokesperson said Monday. Rwandan authorities have been accused of assassinating opponents of President Paul Kagame, who has ruled the country with an iron fist since taking power in the aftermath of the 1994 genocide that claimed 800,000 lives, primarily among the Tutsi community. Robert Kabera, a former sergeant who fled Rwanda several years ago, was not outspoken during his time in the military but grew increasingly opposed to Kagame. His YouTube channel, “Major Robert TV”, which has 144,000 subscribers, included a song praising opposition figure Victoire Ingabire, a rare voice of dissent in Rwanda, who has been repeatedly imprisoned. Ugandan police said they were investigating the “murder of a male adult, (around 50), whose head was cut off, and up to now the head has not yet been recovered”, spokesperson Kituuma Rusoke told reporters on Monday, adding that the body had been identified by relatives as Robert Kabera. The body was found in Luwala, a village near Kampala, and the murder likely took place late on October 16 or early 17, he added. In Uganda, “Robert had no issues with anyone,” his brother, Victor Agaba, told AFP. “Our problem comes from home… The army created a criminal case against him. It was a witch hunt,” he said. Kabera was declared a fugitive after leaving Rwanda, and he was accused of corrupting a minor, which he denied. He is not the first opposition figure in exile to be assassinated. In 2021, a former lieutenant in the Rwandan army, Revocant Karemangingo, was shot dead in Mozambique, where he was suspected of secretly supporting an opposition force. Outspoken opponent Seif Bamporiki was gunned down in South Africa the same year, while a former Rwandan intelligence-chief-turned-critic, Patrick Karegeya, was strangled in his South African hotel room in 2014. Another exile, former general Faustin Kayumba Nyamwasa, who co-founded the Rwanda National Congress (RNC) opposition party with Karegeya, has survived several assassination attempts. item.title: ‘You Cannot Ask Moses To Go Back To Egypt,’ Tinubu Insists No Fuel Subsidy Return
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has reiterated that there will be no return to the fuel subsidy regime, insisting that his administration took a bold and necessary step to reform the country’s economy. Tinubu spoke on Monday during a meeting with the City Boy Movement, a youth-driven political and advocacy group founded to champion his administration’s agenda. “I came, and I removed the subsidy on my first day. Nigeria would have gone bankrupt; there was nothing left to pay for subsidies,” he said. “I could listen to my political opponents promising a return to subsidy.” Drawing a religious analogy, the president added, “I remember my scripture studies, both in the Bible and the Holy Quran. When Moses (Musa) left Egypt, the Red Sea parted and gave way. You cannot ask Moses to go back to Egypt. With your energy and support, we will never go back to Egypt.” The former Lagos State governor commended the organisation for drumming up support for his administration and urged members to take his government’s achievements to the grassroots. “Those of you who are lucky to work with me have given me all the answers needed and the confidence required to see the coming election as a simple matter,” Tinubu stated. “You will go to your campuses, your markets, and your villages. Make sure every young person you know has a PVC and uses it. Tell them what we have done and tell them what we will do. Campaign with your ideas.” President Tinubu announced an end to fuel subsidy during his inauguration in May 2023. The policy shift sparked an immediate hike in petrol pump prices, rising from under ₦200 per litre to current rates hovering between ₦1,350 and ₦1,405 per litre across major filling stations. While the policy has drawn widespread criticism over the heightened cost of living, the president remains firm on his stance. The federal government maintains that the decision is essential to reset the national economy, reassuring citizens that the initial economic hardship will ease over time. The post ‘You Cannot Ask Moses To Go Back To Egypt,’ Tinubu Insists No Fuel Subsidy Return appeared first on Channels Television .
